items.reason: Verifier replies produce timestamped documents under the set’s verify directory.
Sequential verifications retain separate reports; fallback publishes once after resolving the verdict.
The response contract keeps VERDICT first, and report extraction removes that line from substantive replies.
Existing verdict parsing remains unchanged, while malformed replies and absent output are recorded.
Report publication applies equally to PASS, FIXABLE, and NEEDS-HUMAN.
PASS findings must now identify checked evidence and explain each acceptance criterion.
Cached verdict paths bypass report publication.
Invalidation still deletes cache rows without deleting report documents.
Previous reports are excluded from Verifier prompts; prior human notes retain their existing path.
Human acceptance publishes a report without invoking a Verifier.
Human reports include the supplied rationale and the overridden non-PASS verdict.
Human reports use “Accepted by: human” instead of the Verifier authorship label.
Human reports use the shared directory, timestamp format, factual header, and latest-report reader.
The gate preamble displays the latest report’s path and recorded commit without its prose.
The paging action opens the report and returns to the gate loop.
The CLI set detail view displays the latest Verify report pointer.
Artifact ordering places Verify reports above Refine reports.
No agent prompt gains a report pointer; golden changes only update the Verifier response contract.
Missing reports produce no Verify preamble, paging entry, detail pointer, or artifact.
Verification status and badge derivation remain independent of report age.
Status reasons remain truncated, but status-row rendering gains no adjacent report pointer.
Both passes share document rendering, filing, timestamp scanning, header parsing, and pointer machinery.
Refine’s pager failure text changes from “Could not read the refine report” to “Could not read the report.”
Refiner prompt golden files are unchanged.

scores.rationale: Coherent shared machinery and substantial tests, but status-row pointers are missing and a Refine output regression remains; the supplied diff was reviewed without execution.

accepted.behaviour: The one-line truncation of verification reasons stays where a status row has room for only one line, with the pointer to the full document beside it.
accepted.reason: The spec (spec.md:218-220) puts the report pointer beside the one-line findings in a status row. The Reference keeps the one-line findings but puts no pointer beside them. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: Refine's observable behaviour is unchanged: the same directory, the same filename stamps, the same header, and every surface it renders on looks exactly as before.
accepted.reason: The spec (spec.md:20-23, 56-57) says no Refine behaviour that a user can see changes. The Reference changes the Refine paging error from "Could not read the refine report" to "Could not read the report". The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.
